title: At the market
goal: Buy groceries, say quantities and prices, and choose between the partitive article and a quantity word.
bekal: saying amounts with *un kilo de*, *une bouteille de*, *un peu de*
telling *du pain* apart from *un kilo de pain*
wave: Review **Unit 10** first: describe where five places in your own neighborhood are, using *à côté de*, *en face de*, *près de*, *derrière*, *entre*.

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Chez le marchand de fruits
dialogs.intro: Saturday morning at the open-air market. Camille is teaching Budi how to shop.

lines.speaker: Marchand:
lines.id: Good morning! What would you like?

lines.speaker: Camille:
lines.text: Bonjour. Un kilo de pommes, s'il vous plaît.
lines.id: Good morning. A kilo of apples, please.
lines.literal: good-day. one kilo of apples, please.

lines.speaker: Camille:
lines.text: Une demi-livre de fraises et trois bananes.
lines.id: Half a pound of strawberries and three bananas.
lines.literal: a half-pound of strawberries and three bananas.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Est-ce que vous avez des mangues ?

lines.speaker: Marchand:
lines.text: Non, désolé. Ce n'est pas la saison.
lines.id: No, sorry. They're not in season.
lines.literal: no, sorry. it not-is not the season.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Tant pis. Alors un peu de raisin.
lines.literal: so-much worse. then a-little of grapes.

lines.speaker: Marchand:
lines.id: How many? One bunch or two?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Une seule, merci. Ça fait combien ?
lines.id: Just one, thanks. How much is that?
lines.literal: one single, thanks. that makes how-much?

lines.speaker: Marchand:
lines.text: Et deux euros vingt. Merci, bonne journée !
lines.id: And two euros twenty change. Thank you, have a nice day!
lines.literal: and two euros twenty. thanks, good day!

notes: **Quantities always take de without an article.** *Un kilo **de** pommes*, not *un kilo des pommes*. After any quantity word — *kilo, litre, bouteille, paquet, morceau, tranche, peu, beaucoup, assez, trop* — the article drops out and only *de* is left.

**Compare three sentences that all have "apples" in English.** *Je mange **des** pommes* (I eat apples, some unspecified amount), *je mange **un kilo de** pommes* (a kilo), *j'aime **les** pommes* (I like apples, in general). Picking the wrong one won't stop people from understanding you, but it marks you as a beginner right away.
**Et avec ça ?** is the standard line of every French market seller. Literally "and with that?" — it means "anything else?" Answer *c'est tout, merci* when you're done.
**Ça fait combien ?** = how much is it altogether. Its cousins: *c'est combien ?* (for one item) and *je vous dois combien ?* (how much do I owe you — the most polite).

**Prices are read with euros in the middle.** *Douze euros quatre-vingts* = €12.80. The word *centimes* is usually left out. Note also that French writes it 12,80 € — a comma for decimals, not a point.
**Tant pis** = "oh well, never mind", a very common shrug of a phrase. Its opposite is *tant mieux* = "so much the better".

**Une demi-livre** = half a pound, about 250 grams. At a French market *la livre* means 500 grams, not the British or American pound. Market sellers still use it even though the official unit is the kilogram.

grammars.title: Partitive article versus quantity word
body: One decision tree that settles almost every doubt in front of a food noun.
after: Notice that the last three rows all give a bare **de**. This is a big French pattern: as soon as the amount is limited or denied, the article steps aside.
⚠️ One exception that trips people up: after *bien* (meaning "many, a lot") the article stays — *bien **du** monde*, *bien **des** fois*.

grammars.title: Everyday quantities
body: All are followed by *de*, with no article.
after: Before a vowel, *de* becomes *d'*: *une bouteille d'eau*, *une douzaine d'œufs*, *beaucoup d'amis*.
*Combien de…?* follows the same rule: *Combien de pommes ?*, not *combien des pommes*.

blocks.text: ⚠️ *Un œuf* is said uhn-NUHF, but the plural *des œufs* is said day-ZUH — the f disappears. A sound exception that applies only to this word.

blocks.title: Shopping phrases
items: *Je voudrais un kilo de tomates, s'il vous plaît.* — I'd like a kilo of tomatoes, please.
*Vous avez des fraises ?* — Do you have strawberries?
*C'est combien le kilo ?* — How much per kilo?
*Ça fait combien ?* — How much is that altogether?
*Je peux payer par carte ?* — Can I pay by card?

exercises.prompt: Fill in with du, de la, de l', des or de.
Fill in a quantity that makes sense.
Choose le/la/les, du/de la/des, or un/une.
items: Je mange ____ chocolat tous les jours.

answers: du pain — de tomates — du fromage — de légumes — d'eau — de sucre
un litre — une tranche — une douzaine — un paquet — un morceau
le chocolat — du chocolat — un chocolat chaud — le poisson — du poisson
Un kilo de pommes, s'il vous plaît. — Vous avez des fraises ? — Ça fait combien ? — C'est trop cher. — Je ne veux pas de sucre.
